key_insight: A two-stage large language model pipeline can surface many internal inconsistencies in discharge summaries, but reliable use depends on strong context and clinical verification.
clinical_relevance: Automated inconsistency detection could help flag documentation errors that affect clinical reasoning, patient safety, and downstream care decisions.
method: Open-ended candidate inconsistency detection with Gemini 2.5 Pro
Manual expert review of a subset of outputs
evidence_signal: In 3,000 MIMIC-IV-Note discharge summaries, the pipeline found 3,460 candidate inconsistencies and these appeared in 69.7% of admissions.
watch_item: Many flagged items need temporal reasoning, diagnosis evolution, or outpatient-prescribing knowledge, so some apparent contradictions may reflect missing context rather than true errors.
paper_title: Toward Automated Detection of Documentation Inconsistencies in Electronic Health Records
